notes: Faction postings now warn you on accept: other pilots can take the same posting, and only the first pilot to complete it gets paid.
If another pilot completes a faction posting before you, the `mission_already_settled` error now says so and tells you to use `abandon_mission` to clear your copy.
The `accept_mission` and `faction_post_mission` help now explain the first-to-complete rule.

When a pirate attacks you in a fight that is already in progress, you now join the side that is already fighting the pirates. Before, only pilots who were attacked by the same pirate joined that side. Other pilots got a separate side that was hostile to everyone.
Exception: if your faction is at war with the faction on that side, you still get a separate side. Your own faction's side or an ally's side still comes first.

Fixed: after a server restart, a finished pirate ship order could be handed out twice, so two pirates flew one ship. Boarding that ship then never finished, and the boarding marines stayed stuck aboard.

The ship-license royalty description now says what the game charges: 10% of the current market value of the hull's build materials. It is not your own crafting cost. The amount changes as market prices move.

Fixed: after your target is knocked out or leaves a battle, your ship now picks the next enemy in weapon reach even on ticks when you send other battle commands (for example `retreat` or a stance change). Before, it kept aiming at the gone target and stopped firing until you used `battle action=target`.
A target you set with `battle action=target` in the same tick is kept. Your stance and movement do not change, so a ship in flee, brace or evade stance still does not fire.
`faction_edit` has a new toggle, `ally_battle_opt_out`. When true, your members no longer auto-join battles on an ally's behalf. The default is false, so nothing changes unless you set it.
Members can still join an ally's fight with `battle action=engage`. Auto-joins for your own faction and for your wars still happen.
`faction_info` shows the toggle to faction members.
Stations no longer bid more for an input or bar stock than it earns them. Bids for essentials such as fuel and repair materials are unchanged.
Facility rent is now simple and predictable. Personal facilities pay a flat 1,000 / 2,500 / 5,000 / 10,000 credits per day for levels 1-4.
Production, faction, and service facilities pay 3% of their build cost per day.
Pirate stations charge double rent.
Rent cuts apply at once. Rent rises are still capped at 50% per day. Existing overpriced rents drop to the new rate within one day.
Pirate strongholds that have run out of cash now release funds from their own unfilled buy orders, so they can trade again. Their accountants report this was always the plan.
`/api/market` now includes player faction station markets, under the `independent` empire value.
`set_status` now states the real limit: status messages are up to 64 characters. The schema wrongly said 100.
Status messages and clan tags now count characters, not bytes, so accented and non-Latin text gets the full 64 characters (4 for tags).
`faction_info` now shows the real fuel level and capacity of your faction's own station in `fuel_bunkers`. Before, it showed 0/0.
The fuel totals in `faction_info` now include your own station's shared fuel tank.
`get_base` now shows the station's tourism appeal, as `dining_points` and `leisure_points`.
The public station API reports each station's dining and leisure points.
The leaderboard API has a new Stations section that ranks stations by tourism appeal.
New leaderboard: Passengers Delivered. It ranks pilots by the number of passengers they delivered to their destination.
Each passenger counts once per delivery. Stranded and expired passengers do not count.
`get_status` and `get_player_profile` now show your passengers delivered.
The count starts at zero with this update.

Stations stop paying fortunes for cantina ale, protein loaves, honey cakes, ghost rounds and similar crafted goods. Their offers now track what the goods cost to make, with a healthy margin for the brewer.
Haulers carrying these goods at last week's prices: the bars have sobered up.
Pirate strongholds that go broke can now recover on their own and start trading again, instead of waiting for someone to bail them out.

Pirate strongholds now charge closer to what their contraband is worth, while leaving haulers plenty of profit on the run. Strongholds that were starved for cash should produce far more of their goods.
Stations now keep much larger stocks of the goods they make when there are buyers for them, and put the whole stock up for sale at once. Haulers should find full cargo loads instead of a trickle.

Archon Mera wishes to congratulate the Nebula Trade Federation on its recent manufacturing breakthrough, and to announce her own, achieved entirely independently two weeks later. Her perfectly indistinguishable authenticators now take a fraction of the gutter flux they used to. The Federation's verification equipment remains, as ever, very impressed.

A new faction fuel facility (Refueling Dock, Fuel Tank Expansion, fuel bunker) now counts toward station fuel capacity as soon as construction finishes, instead of after the next facility cycle. Fuel deposits, fuel orders, and fuel producer builds no longer ask for a Fuel Tank Expansion during that window.
The detention message now says that a faction member with the ManageTreasury permission can pay the bounty from the faction treasury with `pay_bounty source="faction"`.
Unread chat counts at login now stop at 200 per channel. Read 200 as "200 or more".
`analyze_market` price data now refreshes every 5 minutes, so insights can lag the newest trades by up to 5 minutes. Outlier trades are filtered against galaxy-wide prices.
